AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL

UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF ASSEMBLY
BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT
LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING: YOU MAY ATTEND THE
MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING:
(669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685;
MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER
CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.

  CLOSED SESSION MEETING

  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS

  Ana Valencia, Mayor
  Margarita L. Rios, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember

  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember

 Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter within its
 jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address City
 Council, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms.
 City Council will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. City Council will
 hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
 emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
 consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other
 services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are available at this
 meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be
 made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time
 when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the
 meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has been posted will also
 be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk’s Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard during regular business
 hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the
 City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call
vote. Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

1.  MEETING MINUTES
  Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of March 7, 2023. 825-04

2.  PAYROLL FOR THE PERIOD FEBRUARY 19, 2023 – MARCH 4, 2023
  Staff recommends City Council approve gross payroll in the amount of $1,120,903.23; the payroll check
  numbers 37790 - 37795 and the voucher numbers 316335 – 316789 in the total net amount of
  $830,064.74 for the pay period February 19, 2023 – March 4, 2023.

3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS
  Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period February 28, through March 13, 2023,
  in the total amount of $2,901,392.35. 640

4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY
  Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Mercury Insurance on behalf of Denise Bautista,
  Romeo Platon, Jr., Ayana del Rosario, and Richard Vasquez.

5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – MARCH 8, 2023
  No action is required unless the City Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on
  the item where the Commission’s action was final. 260

6.  PROJECT NO. 7377 – AWARD CONTRACT FOR HOLIFIELD PARK PARKING LOT REPAIRS
  Staff recommends City Council award a construction contract to Pioneer Paving & Landscaping, LLC, of
  Los Angeles, for Holifield Park Parking Lot Repair Project No. 7377, in the amount of $119,693 with up to
  the 25% contingency if necessary; and authorize the City Manager to execute any amendments or change
  orders provided there is funding in the budget and it is within the City Manager’s signing authority; and

City Council, March 21, 2023  Page 3 of 5
   funding on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

7.  AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE AGREEMENTS TO TRANSFER ADMINISTRATION
  OF THE CITY’S OTHER POST EMPLOYMENT BENEFIT AND PENSION 115 TRUST ACCOUNTS
  Staff recommends City Council authorize the City Manager to execute agreements to transfer
  administration of the City’s Other Post Employment Benefit, and Pension Stabilization 115 trust accounts
  to Shuster Advisory Group, LLC; funds’ assets to Charles Schwab Trust Bank; and Alta Trust company as
  directed trustee; and any amendments provided there is funding in budget and it is within the City
  Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

8.  DESIGNATION OF AGENT
  Staff recommends City Council approve the Designation of the Applicants Agent Resolution for Non-State
  Agencies authorizing the City Manager, Deputy City Manager, and/or Director of Public Safety to obtain
  federal financial assistance for any existing or future grant program and to provide California Governors
  Office of Emergency Services for all matters pertaining to such state disaster assistance and agreements
  required.

APPOINTMENTS

9.  ADVISORY BODY APPOINTMENTS
  Staff recommends City Councilmembers either re-appoint current Advisory Body members and/or make
  new appointments for two-year terms expiring on December 31, 2024.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

10. CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING – PROPOSED ACTIVITIES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023/24 ANNUAL
  ACTION PLAN FOR THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT AND HOME INVESTMENT
  PARTNERSHIPS PROGRAM
  Staff recommends City Council and the public provide input of the proposed Community Development
  Block Grant and HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) funding activities for Fiscal Year
  2023/24 Annual Action Plan.

ORDINANCE AND RESOLUTIONS

11. RESOLUTION NO. 23-19 – BUDGET AMENDMENT – ADD LOW AND MODERATE INCOME HOUSING
  ASSET FUNDS FOR CONTRACT SERVICES AND APPROVE ADDITIONAL SERVICES FOR
  CONCEPTUAL LANDSCAPE SERVICES AND ACTIVITIES RELATED TO SITE REMEDIATION FOR
  CITY PROJECT NO. 7859
  Staff recommends City Council:
  a. find that the adoption of Resolution No. 23-19 is not subject to the California Environmental Quality Act
  pursuant to the State California Environmental Quality Act Guidelines, California Code of Regulations,
  Title 14, Chapter 3 15061(b)(3), because the activity is covered by the general rule that California
  Environmental Quality Act applies only to projects that have the potential for causing a significant effect on
  the environment and it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the adoption of this
  Resolution may have a significant effect on the environment;
  b. adopt Resolution No. 23-19, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2022-23 ADOPTED BUDGET TO ADD LOW
  AND MODERATE INCOME HOUSING ASSET FUNDS FOR services FOR CONCEPTUAL LANDSCAPE
  SERVICES AND ACTIVITIES RELATED TO SITE REMEDIATION FOR THE CALIFORNIA YOUTH
  AUTHORITY PROPERTY FOR CITY PROJECT NO. 7859, in the amount of $773,850; and
  c. authorize the City Manager to execute an amendment to the existing agreement with CSG Consultants,
  Inc. for additional identified services and such other services reasonably necessary thereto as determined
  by the City Manager related to the California Youth Authority property, City Project No. 7859, not-to-
  exceed $773,850, provided there is funding in the budget, separate from the existing contract
  compensation, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

 12. RESOLUTION NO. 23-20 - MEMBERSHIP IN THE GATEWAY CITIES AFFORDABLE HOUSING TRUST
  Staff recommends City Council:
  a. authorize the City to join the Gateway Cities Affordable Housing Trust;
  b. adopt Resolution No. 23-20, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK,
  APPROVING, AUTHORIZING, AND DIRECTING CITY EXECUTION OF THE JOINT EXERCISE OF
  POWERS AGREEMENT RELATING TO MEMBERSHIP IN THE GATEWAY CITIES AFFORDABLE
  HOUSING TRUST; and
  c. authorize the Mayor to Execute the Joint Powers Agreement with the Gateway Cities Affordable
  Housing Trust.

REPORTS

13. END OF CALIFORNIA STATE OF EMERGENCY - CHANGES TO TELECONFERENCING PROVISIONS
  Staff recommends City Council review the teleconferencing options provided in this report and give
  direction as to whether the City Council wishes to continue conducting meetings under the provisions of
  AB 361 by imposing or recommending social distancing and making specified findings by a majority vote
  of the City Council.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was
posted on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated March 16, 2023.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
